tool_arguments.query: Micron HBM revenue Q3 fiscal 2026 AI demand

events.content: Micron HBM revenue Q3 fiscal 2026 AI demand

Micron did not disclose a stand-alone total HBM-revenue figure for fiscal Q3 2026; it did disclose that it had already shipped **more than $1 billion of HBM4 revenue**, while HBM4 12-high’s volume ramp was running about twice as fast as the prior HBM3E 12-high ramp. [[1]] 

The broader AI-memory read-through was exceptionally strong: fiscal Q3 revenue was **$41.46 billion**, including record DRAM revenue of **$31.3 billion** (76% of sales, +67% sequentially) and NAND revenue of **$9.9 billion** (+99% sequentially). [[2]] [[3]] 

Data-center revenue exceeded **$25 billion** in the quarter—an annualized run rate above $100 billion—and data-center SSD revenue exceeded **$5 billion**, more than doubling sequentially. [[3]] 

Management attributed the tight market to AI-driven demand, saying DRAM and NAND industry demand continued to significantly exceed supply and that it expected tight conditions to persist beyond calendar 2027. [[3]] 

The demand outlook also strengthened because Micron raised its calendar-2026 server-unit-growth expectation to the **high-teens percentage range**, citing agentic AI’s expansion of memory needs beyond accelerator racks into CPU and storage infrastructure. [[3]] 

For forward visibility, Micron said it had entered 16 strategic customer agreements, with approximately **$100 billion** of remaining performance obligations for agreements signed through and after fiscal Q3, although it cautioned that RPO is based on minimum committed volumes/prices and is not a forecast of total revenue. [[3]] 

In short, the reported **>$1 billion HBM4 figure** confirms a rapid early ramp, while the much larger data-center, DRAM, pricing, supply-tightness, and contracted-demand disclosures indicate that AI demand was the central driver of Micron’s fiscal-Q3 surge rather than HBM alone. [[1]] [[3]]

tool_arguments.query: Micron data center memory revenue Q3 fiscal 2026 AI demand

events.content: Micron data center memory revenue Q3 fiscal 2026 AI demand

**Micron’s AI/data-center memory growth is exceptionally strong and accelerating.** In fiscal Q4 2026 (ended September 3, 2026), Core Data Center Business Unit (CDBU) revenue reached a record **$18.0 billion**, up **56% sequentially** from $11.5 billion and roughly **1,042% year over year** from $1.58 billion; it represented **33% of company revenue**. [[1, 2]] 

The broader data-center exposure is larger than CDBU alone: Cloud Memory Business Unit revenue was **$16.3 billion** in FQ4, meaning CDBU plus Cloud Memory revenue was about **$34.3 billion**, or roughly **63%** of Micron’s $54.23 billion quarterly revenue. [[1]] 

For the full fiscal year 2026, Micron said total data-center revenue increased **fourfold**, while total company revenue rose **256%** to a record **$133.2 billion**. [[3]]

**AI is driving both volume and pricing, not merely unit demand.** Micron attributes CDBU’s FQ4 sequential growth to higher pricing and bit shipments, while CDBU gross margin rose to **90%**, up 290 basis points sequentially, reflecting favorable mix as well as pricing. [[3]] 

The strongest AI-linked categories are DRAM/HBM and data-center SSDs: FQ4 DRAM revenue was **$39.8 billion**, up **343% year over year**, and data-center SSD revenue was nearly **$10 billion**, more than **10×** the prior-year quarter. [[3]] 

Management’s demand thesis is that AI infrastructure requires substantially more memory across accelerator and CPU-based systems; it expects industry data-center DRAM and NAND bit shipments in calendar 2026 to be more than double their level two years earlier. [[4]]

**Investment takeaway:** Micron has shifted from a cyclical PC/mobile-memory recovery to a data-center-led earnings cycle, with AI demand supporting higher memory content, premium HBM/SSD mix, constrained industry supply, and unusually high margins. [[5, 3]] 

The principal risk is that these results depend materially on continued AI-capex strength and tight DRAM/NAND supply-demand conditions; Micron explicitly linked recent price increases to tight industry conditions. [[3]]

Micron did not disclose a stand-alone total HBM-revenue figure for fiscal Q3 2026; it did disclose that it had already shipped **more than $1 billion of HBM4 revenue**, while HBM4 12-high’s volume ramp was running about twice as fast as the prior HBM3E 12-high ramp. [[1]] 

The broader AI-memory read-through was exceptionally strong: fiscal Q3 revenue was **$41.46 billion**, including record DRAM revenue of **$31.3 billion** (76% of sales, +67% sequentially) and NAND revenue of **$9.9 billion** (+99% sequentially). [[2]] [[3]] 

Data-center revenue exceeded **$25 billion** in the quarter—an annualized run rate above $100 billion—and data-center SSD revenue exceeded **$5 billion**, more than doubling sequentially. [[3]] 

Management attributed the tight market to AI-driven demand, saying DRAM and NAND industry demand continued to significantly exceed supply and that it expected tight conditions to persist beyond calendar 2027. [[3]] 

The demand outlook also strengthened because Micron raised its calendar-2026 server-unit-growth expectation to the **high-teens percentage range**, citing agentic AI’s expansion of memory needs beyond accelerator racks into CPU and storage infrastructure. [[3]] 

For forward visibility, Micron said it had entered 16 strategic customer agreements, with approximately **$100 billion** of remaining performance obligations for agreements signed through and after fiscal Q3, although it cautioned that RPO is based on minimum committed volumes/prices and is not a forecast of total revenue. [[3]] 

In short, the reported **>$1 billion HBM4 figure** confirms a rapid early ramp, while the much larger data-center, DRAM, pricing, supply-tightness, and contracted-demand disclosures indicate that AI demand was the central driver of Micron’s fiscal-Q3 surge rather than HBM alone. [[1]] [[3]]

Sources:
[S7.1] Financial results - Micron Investor Relations — https://investors.micron.com/static-files/2354ecda-77a0-4ddd-8462-a631eb491356
[S7.2] Micron Technology, Inc. - Micron Technology, Inc. Reports Record Results for the Third Quarter of Fiscal 2026 — https://investors.micron.com/news/press-release/2026/Micron-Technology-Inc--Reports-Record-Results-for-the-Third-Quarter-of-Fiscal-2026/default.aspx
[S7.3] Micron Technology, Inc. Fiscal Q3 2026 Earnings Call Prepared Remarks — https://investors.micron.com/static-files/631b1a32-5537-46ae-8f40-82e42fc79dfe
